parameters.content:
## Contact Info Search + Match Scoring - Searchbug (api_contact)

Look up a person or business by name, address, phone or email - one at a time or in bulk from a CSV - then score every record for how well it matches the search and how usable the contact actually is. Three tabs out: the records, their address history, and a one-row-per-search summary.

### How it works
1. **Single:** fill in what you know (name + city + state, a company, a phone, or an email). **Bulk:** leave the single fields blank and upload a CSV (first_name, last_name, company_name, address, city, state, zip, phone, email).
2. Validate Input checks each row has enough to search on; Dedupe Searches drops repeat rows so the same query is never paid for twice.
3. The Contact Info API call retries 3x and is throttled to 1 request/second. Check Status routes empty and failed responses to No Records Found.
4. Flatten Records keeps **every** phone, email and address on each record - not just the first - and counts them. Score Match & Completeness then rates each record:
   - **MATCH_SCORE 0-100** - 45 last name + 35 first name + 20 state. Searching by phone or email instead scores 100 when that exact value comes back on the record.
   - **COMPLETENESS_SCORE 0-100** -> **CONTACT_GRADE A-D** - how much of a usable contact you actually got.
   - **FLAGS** - NO_PHONE, NO_EMAIL, NO_ADDRESS, MANY_ADDRESSES, BUSINESS_RECORD, WEAK_MATCH.
5. Three sheets are written:
   - **Contact Info** - one row per record (30 columns)
   - **CI Address History** - one row per address on file
   - **CI Summary** - one row per search: records found, best match, grade, totals.

### How to set up
- [ ] Add your Searchbug CO_CODE + PASS in the HTTP Request (Body Parameters)
- [ ] Connect your OWN Google Sheets account in all three Save nodes
- [ ] Point them at your own spreadsheet and create three tabs:
      - "Contact Info" (30 columns - see Save Contact Detail)
      - "CI Address History" (11 columns - see Save Address History)
      - "CI Summary" (14 columns - see Save Search Summary)
- [ ] Activate and share the form link

### Customization
- Enter ONLY a phone or email for a reverse lookup - the scoring switches to match on that value.
- Change the A-D grade thresholds in Score Match & Completeness.
- CSV headers are case-flexible (first_name / First Name / FIRST_NAME) and zip accepts zip_code or postal_code.

### [!] Privacy
This returns real people's contact details, dates of birth and ages. Use it for legitimate business purposes only, keep the destination sheet access-controlled, and don't use it for FCRA-covered decisions (employment, tenancy, credit, insurance).

## 1. Single or Bulk Input

Single or Bulk? checks whether any single field (name, phone, email or company) was filled. If yes -> Normalize Input; if all blank -> Extract CSV first.

Normalize Input standardizes the column names so both paths share one schema - first_name / First Name / FIRST_NAME all work, and zip also accepts zip_code or postal_code.

## 2. Map, Validate & Dedupe

Set Search Input maps the fields onto the Searchbug parameters. Validate Input routes rows with enough to search on (a full name, a company, a phone or an email); everything else returns an Invalid Input message instead of failing the run.

Dedupe Searches then collapses identical queries into one call and stamps each with a SEARCH_ID that follows it through all three sheets.

## 3. Search & Route

The API node retries 3x and sends 1 request per second, so a long CSV finishes instead of tripping rate limits.

Check Status only passes a response that really has records: no error, STATUS = SUCCESS, and at least one RECORD. A failed call has no STATUS at all - checking it in strict mode throws instead of routing, so this condition is deliberately loose.

Attach Search Context carries the SEARCH_ID past the API call and turns DATA.RECORD into an array - Searchbug returns a bare object when there is exactly one match.

## 4. Flatten & Score

Flatten Records makes one row per record and keeps every phone, email and address on it, with a count for each, so nothing on the record is lost.

Score Match & Completeness then rates the record against what was searched (MATCH_SCORE) and how usable the contact is on its own (COMPLETENESS_SCORE -> CONTACT_GRADE A-D), and raises FLAGS. A low MATCH_SCORE means Searchbug returned a different person with a similar name.

## [!] 5. Three Outputs

**Save Contact Detail** - one row per record (30 columns).
**Save Address History** - one row per address on file, current first.
**Save Search Summary** - one row per search: records found, best match and score, grade, phone / email / address totals, combined flags.

Connect your OWN Google Sheets credential in all three and create the tabs with matching row-1 headers.

Don't use the node menu's Refresh option - it erases the column mapping.

Privacy: real contact data. Keep the sheet access-controlled and out of FCRA-covered decisions.
